exposure: Immediate postpartum intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD) insertion
cohort: The study included 120 women, divided into two groups: 60 who had normal vaginal deliveries and 60 who had C-sections, all of whom received immediate postpartum IUCD insertion.
finding: Immediate postpartum insertion of intrauterine contraceptive devices was found to be an effective and safe method with a low complication rate after both vaginal and cesarean section deliveries.
mod_finding: No significant differences were observed between vaginal and C-section groups for menstrual abnormalities, abdominal pain, vaginal discharge, infection, or expulsion rates, but the IUCD removal rate was higher in the C-section group (11.67%) compared to the vaginal group (3.33%).
